name: Aorun
isnote: Choiniere et al. 2013 described it as a coelurosaur; Wikipedia revision 1388182978 notes that some researchers consider it a carnosaurian, and the article on Shishugounykus lists it only as a possible alvarezsaur of the Shishugou Formation. The backbone placed it in Alvarezsauria.
sum: Small carnivorous theropod from the Late Jurassic Shishugou Formation of Xinjiang, China, known from a skull and partial skeleton.
wsnote: No body size given in the sources consulted.
holotype: IVPP V15709, a skull with lower jaws, a neck vertebra, a dorsal vertebra, three tail vertebrae, the left ulna and hand, the lower ends of both pubes and both lower legs; Xinjiang, China.
biology: The hand is slender, with very thin third and fourth metacarpals, closer to the hands of derived non-avian coelurosaurs than to those of basal theropods; the teeth are unserrated or have very fine serrations only on the back edge. The low tooth count suggests the holotype was a juvenile.
author: Choiniere et al. 2013

sources.text: Choiniere J.N. 2013. A juvenile specimen of a new coelurosaur (Dinosauria: Theropoda) from the Middle–Late Jurassic Shishugou Formation of Xinjiang, People's Republic of China. Journal of Systematic Palaeontology 12(2): 177–215. doi:10.1080/14772019.2013.781067
Qin Z, Clark J, Choiniere J, Xu X 2019. A new alvarezsaurian theropod from the Upper Jurassic Shishugou Formation of western China. Scientific reports. doi:10.1038/s41598-019-48148-7

dates_note: No PBDB record. Wikipedia revision 1388182978 gives about 161.6 Ma (Late Jurassic) without naming a stage; the Oxfordian label is the nearest ICS stage and must be checked.
